tiptap.note: ZERO HERE MEANT NO SCHEMA CHANGE, and the reasoning is worth keeping because the number does not carry it (carve-grammars#310). Nineteen rows were red and none of them was a missing feature. Eight are the smart-typography family, UNSUPPORTED for the reason tiptap/schema-map.json's own `unmapped` section already carried: the engine resolves the source spelling to the resolved character before the bridge sees it, so a node modelling the result would reparse as that character and lose the spelling. The other eleven are folds of what the engine actually emits - all three link spellings arrive as a `link` and all three image spellings as an `image`, the local hard-break block as a `div` with a class where the line block has a type of its own, the braced comment as the one `comment` node, the combined bold-italic spelling as an `emphasis` mark inside a `strong`, and each braced emphasis as the bare one's mark. Nothing was implemented for this surface; the probe was taught to see what was there.

tree-sitter-carve.note: BOTH AXES ARE NOW READ AT THE SAME COMMIT, d61ab29, which is what this surface's `commit` field says; the payload column used to be ahead of it and the note used to say so. The recognition axis moved because markup-carve/tree-sitter-carve#252 named the admonition and the composite figure group, which were the last two GAP rows on this surface (carve-grammars#334). The payload column is measured through the grammar's own native addon plus queries/highlights.scm, resolved the way Neovim and Helix resolve it (highest (#set! priority) wins, later patterns take a tie), so a low-priority pattern nobody paints is not reported as a leak. The four leaks this column carried at 3d12600 are all closed: markup-carve/tree-sitter-carve#249 and #251 took the two `code_block` shapes and the braced comment, #254 the editorial comment across a line break. Every generated document of all four rows now measures inert - 0 of 164 fence shapes, 0 of 469 and 0 of 286. The single-sample column said inert while they leaked, which is why the GENERATED sweep (tests/opaque-payload-test.js, run with CARVE_SURFACE_TREE_SITTER_CARVE) is what this column is read from. ONE CAUTION ABOUT THE EVIDENCE ON THIS SURFACE: before #252 the `admonition` row was not merely unnamed - the nearest word in that grammar was `class_name`, a real rule implementing the dotted class inside an attribute block, so a probe that had scored it would have read the row covered while it was false. The row cites `admonition_type` today, but the evidence for a surface in another repository is re-checked by nobody on a pull request here (tests/construct-ledger-test.js re-probes the four local surfaces only), which is what scripts/surface-drift.mjs reports on.

emacs-carve.note: BOTH AXES ARE NOW READ AT THE SAME COMMIT, db1796b, and the reading before this one described a checkout five merges old (carve-grammars#332). What moved, and why the old note is gone rather than amended: markup-carve/emacs-carve#24 named 28 constructs that had no row and fixed the ATTRIBUTION defect the old note was mostly about - the row for the braced comment cited the delimited comment's own header, so a rule that existed read as a gap under another construct's name. Both `braced_comment` and `editorial_comment` now read IMPLEMENTED, each citing its own rule, and the surface has no GAP rows left. The payload column is measured by fontifying a buffer in batch Emacs and reading back the `face` text property, through the GENERATED sweep (tests/opaque-payload-test.js, run with CARVE_SURFACE_EMACS_CARVE) rather than through one sample per construct - which is the distinction that mattered here, since the single-sample column called every row inert while six leaked. All six recorded leaks are closed: markup-carve/emacs-carve#28 bounded a verbatim payload by its paragraph rather than by its line, taking the two comment rows and the three code-span rows, and `comment_block` had already been inert since #24. markup-carve/emacs-carve#29 additionally closed the UNTERMINATED fence, which was a residual rather than a ledger row. ONE SHAPE STILL LEAKS AND IS NOT A LEDGER CELL: a comment whose continuation line opens a block is broken by the block rule, pinned in the RESIDUALS table of that file alongside prism and intellij-carve, because it needs a container model rather than a wider rule.
